title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is §38 (relabelled '29 bis') of the continuation of La Longue Marche, numbered pages 293–650 (the previous page is the table of contents, page 4). The title announces an explicit determination of an isomorphism π'_{0,3} ≅ \check{\mathfrak S}^+_{0,3}, and of its non-oriented variant. Here π'_{0,3} is the orbifold ('signed') fundamental group of the projective line with three marked points carrying a signature. The non-oriented variant π'^~_{0,3} is described as 'the pro-cartographic group, bi-Galois, non-oriented'. These groups are presumably the oriented and non-oriented (profinite) cartographic groups. The non-oriented one would be the extension by Z/2 corresponding to complex conjugation (the full cartographic group generated by involutions).

To prepare this, he goes back to a proposition of an earlier section (p. 262). The setting:
- X is an (orientable) surface and G is a discrete group acting properly on it.
- Each stabilizer G_x preserves orientation and acts faithfully near x.
- Y = X/G carries the 'signature' d = d(X/Y), given by the ramification indices d_b at the branch locus Y^! = Supp d.

There is then an isomorphism (1): π = π_1((X,G),x) ≅ π_1((Y,d),y) = π'. In modern terms, the equivariant fundamental group (the extension of G by π_1(X)) equals the orbifold fundamental group of the quotient orbifold.

Local structure on the quotient side:
- For each branch point b ∈ Y^!, the 'local subgroups' form a conjugacy class of subgroups that are quotients of Z/d_b.
- More precisely there is a canonical exterior homomorphism (2): T_b ⊗ Z/d_b → π'.
- It is obtained by passing to the quotient from the exterior homomorphism (3): T_b → π_1(Y∖Y^!) → π_1((Y,d)).
- Here T_b is the free rank-one Z-module of 'twisted integers' at b. This is the canonical generator-free local H_1 of a punctured disc around b, i.e. the topological analogue of Ẑ(1).

Local structure on the cover side:
- For a ∈ X over b, the stabilizer G_a is cyclic of order d_a = d_b.
- There is a canonical isomorphism (4): G_a ≅ T_a ⊗ Z/d_a ≅ T_b ⊗ Z/d_b, with T_a ≅ T_b canonically. This is the rotation action of G_a on the tangent plane at a, normalized via twisted integers.

The next page continues:
- Points a in the fixed locus correspond to π_1(X)-conjugacy classes of splittings k_a : G_a → π_1((X,G),x) of 1 → π_1(X) → π_1(X,G) → G → 1, for X ≠ S².
- Passing to exterior homomorphisms, one gets a Proposition: Y^! is in bijection with the 'maximal' exterior homomorphisms Γ → π lifting inclusions of nontrivial (necessarily cyclic) subgroups Γ ⊂ G.
- Purpose: identify canonically, with cyclotomic-type normalization, the inertia/torsion data of the orbifold group. This is needed to write the explicit isomorphism with the (pro)cartographic group, compatibly with orientation-reversal and, ultimately, the Galois action.
errors: No mathematical error visible. The exclusion X ≠ S² (on the next page) is necessary, since for spherical quotients the correspondence between splittings and fixed points fails (finite π). Faithfulness of the local action is correctly assumed, so that d_a = |G_a|.
Minor: calling the images of T_b ⊗ Z/d_b 'quotients of Z/d_b' is correct. In fact they are injective (isomorphic to Z/d_b) except in the bad spherical cases; this is not yet stated on this page.

ideas.what: Isomorphism between the equivariant fundamental group π_1((X,G),x) and the orbifold fundamental group of (X/G, signature d)
ideas.modern_name: orbifold fundamental group of the quotient orbifold [X/G]
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Poincaré/Fuchsian groups; Thurston's orbifolds, 1970s); Haefliger for orbifold π_1
ideas.where_published: Related ideas in SGA1 (tame fundamental group with ramification) and La Longue Marche (1981, circulated)

ideas.what: Canonical exterior homomorphism T_b ⊗ Z/d_b → π' from 'twisted integers' at a branch point (generator-free inertia)
ideas.modern_name: local inertia subgroups with canonical Z(1)-type generator (topological cyclotomic twist)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck–Murre / SGA1 for the tame inertia ≅ Ẑ'(1); standard in the dessins/GT literature
ideas.where_published: SGA1 (tame ramification), Esquisse d'un programme (implicitly), La Longue Marche

ideas.what: Canonical isomorphism of a cyclic stabilizer G_a with T_a ⊗ Z/d_a via rotation of the tangent plane
ideas.modern_name: rotation character / canonical identification of the stabilizer with μ_d-type twisted group

ideas.what: Bijection between branch points of Y and conjugacy classes of maximal lifts of finite subgroups (splittings over G_a ↔ fixed points)
ideas.modern_name: torsion in Fuchsian/orbifold groups conjugate into elliptic stabilizers; discrete analogue of the fixed-point/section correspondence
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical for Fuchsian groups. The profinite analogue is discussed in Grothendieck's 1983 letter to Faltings and proved later (e.g. via goodness of surface groups)
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983) discusses the profinite fixed-point analogue

ideas.what: Plan to identify π'_{0,3} and its non-oriented 'bi-Galois' version with the (pro)cartographic groups
ideas.modern_name: oriented/non-oriented cartographic groups C_2^+, C_2 and their profinite completions (dessins d'enfants)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984); Jones–Singerman for maps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme; La Longue Marche

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful but standard set-up: equivariant π_1 equals orbifold π_1, canonical twisted inertia, and stabilizers identified with T ⊗ Z/d. All of this is classical or folklore. Its role in the explicit cartographic isomorphism is consistent with Grothendieck's known programme.
transcription_corrections: Header: '29.(bis)' is written above the title; the target group is a check-accented script letter (likely \check{\mathfrak S}^+_{0,3} / \mathfrak S_{0,3}), not a plain \mathfrak S.
'(gr. pro-cartographique bi-galoisé non orienté)' — the insertion 'bi-galoisé non orienté' is under 'pro-cartographique'.
'une classe d'extensions[?] canonique' should read roughly 'un hom extérieur canonique' (singular), consistent with 'déduit par passage au quotient de l'hom ext (3)'.
The insertion under 'groupe' reads like 'G_n' or similar; it is unclear and probably not 'G_m'.
The insertion under 'revenir sur la prop.' is illegible; it is not clearly 'orienté'.
